end.summary:
• Common animal diets were practised: plant-eaters, meat-eaters, and animals that eat both; a why or new-situation check is still needed.
• Manav built and read food chains with arrows, including grass → grasshopper → frog → snake and algae → larvae → fish → kingfisher; this was shown on a new-situation question.
• Effects of removing one living thing were practised; some predictions were right, but this is not steady yet.
• Manav explained that plants make their own food using sunlight and start food chains; this was shown on a new-situation question.
end.parentNote: Asha practised animal diets, food-chain order and arrows, and what may happen when one part of a chain is removed. Manav used the method of following who eats whom to build chains, and connected sunlight with plants making their own food. Predictions after removing an organism were mixed and need more practice next time; ask them to explain one food chain and predict one change at home.
